chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umair, from Al-As ibn Rasin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: 'The Sufyani will rule for the duration of a woman's pregnancy after his emergence over the five provinces.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'I seek forgiveness of Allah, [it will be] the duration of a camel's pregnancy, and it is from the inevitable matter that must occur.'

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيّ: The Sufyani, a specific leader in Shia eschatology who emerges before the reappearance of Imam Mahdi.
key_terms.الظُّهُور: Emergence or appearance, specifically referring to the emergence of the Sufyani.
key_terms.الْأَمْرُ الْمُحْتَوَم: The inevitable matter or decree that must occur.
key_terms.الْكُور: Provinces or regions, specifically referring to the five major provinces under his control.
key_terms.حَمْلُ امْرَأَةٍ: Duration of a woman's pregnancy, used here as a measure of time for the reign.
key_terms.حَمْلُ جَمَلٍ: Duration of a camel's pregnancy, a longer period used for comparison.

ai.seo_question: How long will the Sufyani rule according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* outlines the brief but significant reign of the Sufyani, specifying his control over the 'five provinces' (Kawar) for a duration comparable to a woman's pregnancy. The Imam’s subsequent remark regarding a camel's pregnancy highlights the scholarly debate on whether this signifies a shorter or longer period, ultimately affirming the inevitability (al-Amr al-Mahdum) of this eschatological event within Shia tradition.
